channel.title: Knowledge-Graph on Junho Lee
channel.description: Recent content in Knowledge-Graph on Junho Lee

item.title: DataNexus Architecture: Four Layers and Two Flows
item.description: Why ontology-based routing instead of a single NL2SQL pipeline — and what the second flow, from Pull to Push, looks like

item.title: NVIDIA Auto-Ontology: A Semantic Context Layer for Enterprise Text-to-SQL
item.description: NVIDIA’s open-source Auto-Ontology compiles database metadata into human-certified business terms, verified SQL formulas, and join graphs exposed over MCP.

item.title: Semantica: Knowledge Graph Tracking for AI Decisions and Provenance
item.description: Semantica records data facts and AI decisions as knowledge graph nodes with W3C PROV-O export and rule-based reasoning, alongside current Rete engine limitations.

item.title: 5. Data Modeling in the LLM Era
item.description: Notes from reading all seven references cited in a post arguing that data modeling comes before code. Covers the principles that outlasted three generations of tooling, four history-tracking patterns used in production, and organizational debt — the slowest debt to surface.

item.title: How AI Engineers Validate Agent Outputs Using Ontologies
item.description: Explore why production engineers pair Agentic AI loops with ontology-backed deterministic validation to catch hallucinations and enforce business rules.

item.title: Turning a Codebase into a Queryable Knowledge Graph with graphify
item.description: graphify combines local tree-sitter AST parsing and semantic document analysis to build a queryable codebase knowledge graph without a vector database.

item.title: Microsoft Ontology Playground: Free Browser Tool for Learning Ontologies
item.description: Explore Microsoft’s free Ontology Playground for designing interactive entity-relationship graphs, importing/exporting RDF files, and prototyping GraphRAG schemas.

item.title: Building an AI Agent Pre-Ontology from Meeting Minutes with Tiro
item.description: Agent reliability depends on shared organizational context. See how AI note-taker Tiro extracts entities from meetings into a pre-ontology wiki that powers lean teams.

item.title: Why AI Adoption Quotes Hit 800M KRW and How to Break Past AX Stage 2
item.description: Inflated AI project quotes stem from misdiagnosing Stage 2 companies as Stage 4-5 ready. Extracting field workflows into an ontology breaks the bottleneck.

item.title: LLM Graph Builder: Turning Unstructured Files into Neo4j Knowledge Graphs
item.description: Open-source LLM Graph Builder extracts nodes and relationships from PDFs, videos, and web pages into Neo4j for hybrid vector and graph querying.

item.title: Jikji: Deterministic File Maps and Local Search for AI Agents
item.description: Open-source Jikji replaces heavy vector databases and wasteful CLI grep loops with cached file maps, LLM Wiki pages, and deterministic graph routing.

item.title: LLM Wiki: A Desktop Knowledge Base Built on Karpathy's Wiki Pattern
item.description: LLM Wiki implements Andrej Karpathy’s incremental wiki pattern as a desktop app, turning raw documents into a persistent knowledge graph.

item.title: Real-Time GraphRAG Without Prebuilt Knowledge Graphs: LogicRAG
item.description: LogicRAG skips expensive offline graph construction by building query-time reasoning DAGs with topological sorting and rolling memory.

item.title: Making AI Context Relationships Explicit with Graphs
item.description: How explicit graph edges cut token waste and prevent state loss in long-running AI workflows, illustrated through codegraph and ActiveGraph.

item.title: 11. Designing Chat UIs for Uncertain AI Answers
item.description: How DataNexus shows answer evidence: SQL, Runtime Trace, fallback state, permission scope, sources, and the knowledge graph alongside the answer.

item.title: RAG-Anything: Multimodal RAG Across Text, Images, Tables, and Equations
item.description: HKUDS’s LightRAG-based framework links text, images, tables, and formulas in a dual graph, posting gains on DocBench and MMLongBench.

item.title: 10. Spider 72%: The Dataset, Not the Model, Shapes the Error Profile
item.description: Switching to Pro actually dropped accuracy by 8%p. I categorized 19 errors into 6 types and ran the same pipeline on Spider. The distributions were completely different. DB characteristics determine the error profile more than the model does.

item.title: 8. 30-Question Retail Sample at 80%: Four PDCA Cycles
item.description: After wiring up the router, I ran a 30-question benchmark and pushed NL2SQL EX (Execution Accuracy) from 66.67% to 80%. Here’s what I fixed across four cycles and where things broke.

item.title: 7. When a Question Comes In, Who Decides the Routing?
item.description: The term definitions are done. But when a user asks a question, who decides whether to search the graph, write SQL, or run a vector search? Things I ran into while designing the router.

item.title: 6. When You Don't Have to Build Agent Infra Yourself, Harnesses Become Obsolete. What About the Ontology?
item.description: Shortly after the Conway leak, Anthropic officially launched Claude Managed Agents. As agent infrastructure gets absorbed into platforms, here’s why DataNexus’s ontology layer remains safe.

item.title: 3. On-Site GEO Technical Architecture - From Product DB to JSON-LD
item.description: How product master DB data flows through a 3-stage pipeline to become JSON-LD in your HTML <head>. Covers the pipeline architecture and SSR-based automated deployment.

item.title: korean-law-mcp: Statute Lookup and Citation Verification via Open API
item.description: How korean-law-mcp wraps 42 Korean Ministry of Government Legislation APIs into 10 tools for statute lookup, citation checks, and version diffs.

item.title: 1. What Is GEO - AI Citation Strategy Beyond SEO
item.description: Only 9% of Google’s top 10 pages are cited by AI. In an era where SEO rankings no longer guarantee AI citations, we break down the three core principles of GEO and their academic foundations.

item.title: 4. Why We Added a SKOS Compatibility Layer
item.description: Why we chose SKOS to connect the DataNexus ontology with external systems. Designing a compatibility layer between LPG and RDF – two different graph models.

item.title: 3. Can DataHub's Glossary Work as an Ontology?
item.description: We tried using DataHub’s Business Glossary as an ontology store. What worked, what didn’t, and how we worked around it.

item.title: 2. How We Chose These 4 Open-Source Tools
item.description: How we decided on DataHub + Vanna + ApeRAG + DozerDB for DataNexus. What got eliminated from the candidate list, and why.

item.title: 1. Why We're Building DataNexus
item.description: The structural problems with enterprise data analytics, and why we decided to build an ontology-based data agent platform.
